plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with conservative limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.
Sell METU, MSFU, and PLTU to reduce high-beta exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by cutting leveraged and high-beta positions. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to small positions, and trim high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU).
Buy SPXS at 4% to introduce a small inverse hedge against broad market downturns.
This plan balances growth potential with risk management, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
Overall concentration is reduced towards 25%.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5%/month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a small hedge. Expect moderate volatility and a more diversified risk profile.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to existing leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to increase exposure.
Buy SPXS at 6% to provide a larger inverse hedge against potential downturns.
This plan leans into higher-scoring setups and uses leverage for aggressive growth.
A smaller cash buffer is maintained, and strict stops are crucial.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk, daily leverage decay, and the need for strict stop discipline to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Sell all high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
A cash buffer will be maintained for stability.
income.read: This income plan aims for approximately 1%/month, focusing on steady distributions. It significantly reduces growth-oriented and leveraged positions for stability. While prioritizing income, remember distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
